lines: כִּי הַשֹּׂשָׂוֹן חֵלֶק עוֹלֵי דֶּרֶךְ הַשָּׁמַיִם
נָשְׂאוּ אֶת־הַצְּלָב וְלֹא בֹשׁוּ מִמֶּנִּי בִּבְנֵי אָדָם
וְלֹא בִקְשׁוּ חֵלֶק זוּלָתִי שְׁמִי הַנִּבְזֶה
הִנְנִי בָא מְהֵרָה, וּפִתְאֹם אָבוֹא לָכֶם
אַךְ קַוֵּה־לוֹ וְצַפֵּה דַּקָּה אַחַר דַּקָּה

review: The hymn is the pilgrim's colloquy with the Redeemer: 1:1–5 is Ps 42:2 with 1 Pet 1:19 and Col 2:14, 2:1–5 is Ps 126:1–3 with Matt 25:34 (בְּרוּכִים) and Rev 7:17, 3:1–5 is Matt 10:32–33 with Rom 8:17 and Rev 3:21 and 4:4, 4:1–5 is Isa 35:4 with Col 1:13 and John 14:2, and 5:1–5 is Rev 22:7,12 with Matt 24:44 and Rev 19:7–9.

3:1–2 keep the two halves of the Arabic contrast (bearing the cross / seeking no other portion than the despised name) on two long lines; the Hebrew uses בֹּשׁ (Ps 22:6) for 'unashamed' and בָּזָה for 'despised', because both are the psalm's and the martyr-word's own vocabulary.

4:4–5 כִּי הִנֵּה הֲכִינוֹתִי אֶצְלִי … לְךָ מָדוֹר — the Arabic أَعْدَدْتُ عِنْدِيَ … لَكَ مَنْزِلًا splits the preparation and the abode; the Hebrew keeps the split and uses מָדוֹר, the dwelling-word of Ps 89:48 and Job 8:18, so the promise is a place and not a mood.

5:2 הִשָּׁמֶר־לְךָ פֶּן־תִּשְׁכַּח — the Arabic إِيَّاكَ أَنْ تَنْسَى is an emphatic warning ('beware lest you forget'); the Hebrew reproduces the Semitic construction with הִשָּׁמֶר־לְךָ … פֶּן, as Deut 4:9 and 8:11 do, rather than weakening it to a plain prohibition.
